caption: What if you never got tired? Marathon runners usually 'hit the wall' around 30 km, when the glycogen stored in their muscles and liver runs low. With no tiredness, jogging at 10 km/h day and night would cover 240 km every 24 hours. But you'd still need fuel: running burns roughly 1 calorie per kg per km, so a 60 kg person would need about 14,400 calories a day, roughly 60 samosas. Humans are built for distance: nearly 4 million sweat glands keep us cool, and early hunters may have jogged after animals for hours until the animals tired. At that pace, Delhi to Mumbai (about 1,400 km) takes about 6 days. But your brain still needs sleep, and real tiredness is a safety signal, so don't ignore it. Plot twist: an Amur falcon called Apapang, weighing about 150 g, flew about 3,100 km nonstop across the Arabian Sea in 76 hours. What would YOU do with endless energy? 👇
